coupling: The invariant 'has_alpha implies dst_a != NULL' entering ImportYUVAFromRGBA_C (src/dsp/yuv.c) was previously enforced twice: (a) inside the DSP function by 'has_alpha &= dst_a != NULL', and (b) by the EmitRowsYUVA caller (src/dec/vp8l_dec.c), which only computed has_alpha inside 'if (dst_a)'. Commit d5fa6c9's edit removes the DSP-side mask as redundant -- at that commit both call sites still guarantee the invariant (EmitRowsYUVA gates has_alpha on dst_a; the encoder passes a non-NULL picture->a whenever has_alpha=1), so the removal alone is benign and all inputs behave identically. Commit 47dbfea's edit hoists the has_alpha/CheckNonOpaque computation out of the 'if (dst_a)' guard so content alpha is detected independently of the MODE_YUV output-plane gate -- at that commit the DSP-side mask still neutralizes has_alpha when dst_a is NULL, so this alone is also benign. Composed, decoding a lossless WebP with non-opaque alpha into a MODE_YUV external buffer (47dbfea legitimately forces dst_a=NULL for MODE_YUV) lets has_alpha=1 reach WebPExtractAlpha with dst_a=NULL: a NULL-pointer write (CWE-476) in ExtractAlpha_SSE2 <- ImportYUVAFromRGBA_C <- EmitRowsYUVA <- ProcessRows <- VP8LDecodeImage, reached purely through the public WebPDecode API. Neither edited commit's diff is wrong in isolation; the fix must restore the cross-module invariant (e.g. pass has_alpha masked by dst_a at the EmitRowsYUVA call site, or re-mask in the DSP), i.e. it must reason about both commits together. Verified: original batch 0/50 crashes, e1-only 0/50, e2-only 0/50, both edits 50/50 ASan aborts.

pocs.entry_point: WebPDecode (webp/decode.h) with external MODE_YUV WebPYUVABuffer; input bytes produced in-probe via WebPEncode (webp/encode.h) lossless from crafted RGBA with non-opaque alpha
